papers.title: PoolParty: streamlined design of DNA sequence libraries in Python.
papers.abstract: Computationally designed DNA sequence libraries are essential components of massively parallel reporter assays (MPRAs), deep mutational scanning (DMS) experiments, and other multiplex assays of variant effect (MAVEs). They are also increasingly used in silico to analyze genomic AI models. Designing these libraries, however, remains tedious and error-prone due to the scarcity of purpose-built software.
papers.summary: PoolParty is a new Python package that streamlines the design of computationally generated DNA sequence libraries used in massively parallel reporter assays, deep mutational scanning, and other multiplex assays of variant effect. It addresses the current lack of purpose-built software, which makes library design tedious and error-prone, and also supports in silico analysis of genomic AI models.

papers.title: Assessing the predictive potential of the Holstein bovine sperm methylome for bull fertility using machine learning.
papers.abstract: Bull fertility is a key parameter in the dairy cattle industry, with significant economic implications. DNA methylation is an epigenetic mark essential for fertility, and recent works have highlighted sperm DNA methylation as a promising source of biomarkers for male fertility, but no operational tool has been developed for predicting bull fertility based on DNA methylation. Here, we leveraged existing methylation data to evaluate the potential of DNA methylation for predicting bull fertility with machine learning models.
papers.summary: This study used machine learning to test whether DNA methylation patterns in Holstein bull sperm can predict bull fertility. Leveraging existing methylation data, the authors evaluated the predictive potential of these epigenetic marks as biomarkers for male fertility in dairy cattle. The work aims to move toward an operational tool for fertility prediction based on sperm DNA methylation.

papers.title: Microbiology Galaxy Lab: a community-driven gateway for reproducible and FAIR analysis of microbiological data.
papers.abstract: The explosion of microbial omics data has outpaced the ability of many researchers to analyse it, with complex tools and limited computational resources creating barriers to discovery. To address this gap, we present the Microbiology Galaxy Lab (MGL): a free, globally accessible, community-supported platform that combines state-of-the-art analytical power with user-friendly accessibility. Supported by the Galaxy and global microbiology communities, this platform integrates over 315 tool suites and 115 curated workflows, enabling comprehensive metabarcoding, (meta)genomic, (meta)transcriptomic,
papers.summary: The authors present the Microbiology Galaxy Lab (MGL), a free, community-supported web platform that bundles over 315 tool suites and 115 curated workflows for reproducible, FAIR analysis of microbial omics data. It aims to lower computational and technical barriers for microbiologists working with metabarcoding, (meta)genomic, and (meta)transcriptomic data. The platform is backed by the Galaxy ecosystem and global microbiology communities.

papers.title: MitImpact 4: a genome-wide resource for the interpretation of coding and non-coding mitochondrial DNA variants.
papers.abstract: Mitochondrial DNA variants are a frequent cause of inherited disease, yet their computational interpretation has focused almost exclusively on the 13 protein-coding genes. Variants in tRNA and rRNA genes, which carry a disproportionate share of the known pathogenic alleles, have remained a diagnostic blind spot, because their effect depends on RNA structure rather than on protein sequence and few dedicated predictors exist. MitImpact 4 removes this asymmetry. The database now covers all 49 704 single-nucleotide variants that can occur in the mitochondrial genome and reports their functional co
papers.summary: MitImpact 4 is a database that expands mitochondrial DNA variant interpretation from just the 13 protein-coding genes to the entire mitochondrial genome, covering all 49,704 possible single-nucleotide variants. This addresses a diagnostic blind spot for tRNA and rRNA gene variants, which are disproportionately pathogenic but previously lacked dedicated computational predictors because their effects depend on RNA structure rather than protein sequence.

papers.title: Experimental benchmarking of in silico annotations at prostate cancer risk loci and hypothesis-generating cross-cancer prioritisation of ovarian risk variants.
papers.abstract: Genome-wide association studies (GWAS) have identified numerous non-coding risk variants for prostate and ovarian cancers, yet determining which are regulatorily active and which target genes they control remains challenging. We re-analysed a dinucleotide-barcode massively parallel reporter assay (DiR-seq) of 208 bi-allelic prostate cancer risk single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) in three prostate cancer cell lines under false-discovery-rate (FDR) control, identifying 50 regulatory SNPs at FDR < 0.10 (30 at FDR < 0.05), including 9 shared by at least two cell lines. Benchmarking standard in
papers.summary: The authors re-analyzed a massively parallel reporter assay (DiR-seq) testing 208 prostate cancer risk SNPs across three cell lines, identifying 50 regulatory SNPs at FDR < 0.10. They then benchmarked common in silico annotation tools against these experimental results and applied the approach to prioritize ovarian cancer risk variants by cross-cancer comparison. The work provides an experimentally grounded benchmark for computational regulatory variant prediction and a hypothesis-generating framework for non-coding risk variant prioritization.

papers.title: rustybam: a composable toolkit for alignment analysis and visualization with SafFire.
papers.abstract: We present rustybam, a Rust-based command-line toolkit for CIGAR-aware manipulation of PAF and BAM alignments, and SafFire, a browser-based tool for interactive genome comparison visualization with annotation overlays. rustybam's composable subcommands provide overlap resolution, coordinate liftover, alignment splitting at structural variants, scaffolding, and identity statistics.
papers.summary: rustybam is a Rust-based command-line toolkit that performs CIGAR-aware manipulation of PAF and BAM alignments, offering composable subcommands for overlap resolution, coordinate liftover, splitting alignments at structural variants, scaffolding, and identity statistics. It is paired with SafFire, a browser-based tool for interactive genome comparison visualization with annotation overlays. Together they provide a fast, modular workflow for alignment analysis and comparative genomics visualization.

papers.title: KmerSignificance score: A discriminative and biologically informed framework for viral k-mer prioritization.
papers.abstract: Distinguishing closely related viral strains requires identifying genomic regions where subtle sequence differences carry biological significance. While k-mer-based approaches offer computational efficiency for genome analysis, existing methods lack standardized frameworks for evaluating which k-mers are most informative. Current selection strategies focus primarily on statistical discriminative power without integrating biological context. We introduce KmerSignificance Score (KSS), a k-mer prioritization framework combining three components: an information-theoretic method measuring strain-di
papers.summary: The paper introduces the KmerSignificance Score (KSS), a framework for prioritizing viral k-mers that combines statistical discriminative power with biological context, addressing the gap in standardized methods for identifying informative k-mers. KSS integrates an information-theoretic measure of strain discrimination with additional biologically informed components, enabling better selection of k-mers for distinguishing closely related viral strains.

papers.title: An Integrated Framework Coupling Hierarchical Hyperspectral i-trait Screening, Gene Identification, and Functional Validation for Genetic Dissection of Salt Tolerance in Cotton.
papers.abstract: Cotton is an economically pivotal fiber crop worldwide, but its growth and yield are critically limited by soil salinity. Salt tolerance is a complex quantitative trait, and conventional destructive phenotyping methods have long hindered the efficiency and accuracy of gene discovery and genetic dissection. To overcome this phenotyping bottleneck and establish a streamlined workflow from phenotype to gene, we developed an integrated framework coupling dynamic hyperspectral phenomics, hierarchical trait selection, genome-wide association study (GWAS), and functional validation, and applied it to
papers.summary: This study develops an integrated framework that combines dynamic hyperspectral imaging, hierarchical trait selection, GWAS, and functional validation to dissect salt tolerance in cotton. The approach overcomes the limitations of destructive phenotyping by enabling non-invasive, high-throughput screening of salt-tolerance traits, leading to the identification and validation of candidate genes. This provides a streamlined phenotype-to-gene workflow for complex quantitative traits in crops.

papers.title: [Genome-wide identification, expression profiling, and natural allelic variation analysis of the ckx genes in sorghum (Sorghum bicolor)].
papers.abstract: Cytokinin (CK) is one of the essential plant hormones, and cytokinin oxidase (CKX) is the key enzyme for CK degradation. Currently, the ckx gene family of rice (Oryza sativa) and maize (Zea mays) have been characterized, while a genome-wide analysis of the ckx gene family in sorghum (Sorghum bicolor) has not been reported. This study aims to identify the Sbckx gene family in sorghum, analyze its evolutionary characteristics and expression patterns, and screen for key genes. A combined approach of bioinformatics analysis and experimental validation was utilized to examine sorghum subjected to a
papers.journal: Sheng wu gong cheng xue bao = Chinese journal of biotechnology
papers.summary: This study performs the first genome-wide identification and characterization of the cytokinin oxidase (ckx) gene family in sorghum, including phylogenetic analysis, expression profiling, and natural allelic variation analysis. The authors identify Sbckx family members and screen for key genes potentially involved in cytokinin regulation, using both bioinformatics and experimental validation.

papers.title: SomatiX: accurate and efficient somatic SNV detection from matched tumor-normal long-read DNA sequencing.
papers.abstract: Accurate somatic single-nucleotide variant (SNV) calling from matched tumor-normal long-read DNA sequencing remains challenging because sequencing errors, variable tumor purity, tumor-in-normal contamination, and low variant allele fractions (VAFs) can obscure tumor-specific signals. Although recent deep-learning methods have improved long-read somatic variant calling, robust low-VAF detection and efficient genome-scale analysis remain important methodological challenges.
papers.summary: SomatiX is a new computational tool for detecting somatic single-nucleotide variants by comparing matched tumor and normal DNA sequencing data generated with long-read technologies. It aims to overcome key obstacles such as sequencing errors, low tumor purity, and low variant allele fractions, while remaining efficient at genome scale. The work addresses a recognized gap in robust, accurate long-read somatic variant calling.

papers.title: A Practical Guide to Dereplication in Natural Products Metabolomics.
papers.abstract: Liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS)-based metabolomics has become a central approach for characterizing the chemical diversity of biological systems, particularly in natural product discovery. However, the scale and complexity of untargeted LC-MS/MS datasets present a persistent challenge: only a small fraction of detected features can be confidently assigned to known structures, leaving much of the metabolome unexplored. Dereplication and annotation tools have rapidly expanded to address this bottleneck, including molecular networking, spectral library matching, substruc
papers.summary: This paper provides a practical guide to dereplication strategies in natural products metabolomics, addressing the challenge that only a small fraction of LC-MS/MS features can be confidently annotated. It surveys and compares tools such as molecular networking, spectral library matching, and substructure annotation, offering guidance on how to apply them to untargeted datasets.

papers.title: Aircraft and Airport Wastewater Surveillance for Public Health Preparedness Demands an Integrated and Sustainable Approach.
papers.abstract: As domestic and international travel has expanded, the risk of the cross-border dissemination of infectious pathogens has increased, as clearly evidenced during the COVID-19 pandemic. Aircraft- and airport-based wastewater surveillance can provide timely, aggregate evidence of pathogen circulation among mobile populations and may complement clinical, genomic, and syndromic surveillance at points of entry. The strongest evidence for this approach comes from SARS-CoV-2 RNA detection and variant monitoring in aircraft lavatory wastewater, airport terminal wastewater, and airport-associated wastew
papers.summary: This perspective argues that wastewater surveillance at airports and on aircraft can provide early, aggregated signals of pathogen circulation among travelers, complementing clinical and genomic surveillance at borders. The strongest evidence so far comes from detecting SARS-CoV-2 RNA and variants in lavatory and terminal wastewater, but the authors stress that the approach needs to be integrated and sustainable to be useful for public health preparedness.

papers.title: XenoMix: Estimating mouse content from DNA methylation data of Patient-Derived Xenograft models.
papers.abstract: DNA methylation microarrays enable cost-effective, high-throughput profiling of human and mouse samples and are widely used to study epigenetic alterations in cancer. Patient-Derived Xenograft (PDX) models complement this approach by preserving primary tumor characteristics while enabling in vivo studies of drug response and therapy resistance. However, it remains difficult to quantify mouse DNA contamination in PDX DNA methylation data generated using microarrays. We present XenoMix, a light-weight computational tool for quantifying mouse DNA contamination directly from DNA methylation data i
papers.summary: XenoMix is a lightweight computational tool that estimates the proportion of mouse DNA contamination in DNA methylation microarray data from Patient-Derived Xenograft (PDX) models. It addresses the common problem of mixed human-mouse signal in PDX epigenomic profiling, enabling researchers to quantify and account for mouse stromal contamination without additional experimental steps.

papers.title: Serial Cryosectioning for the Spatial Transcriptomics of Plant Tissues.
papers.abstract: Spatial transcriptomics enables genome-wide gene expression profiling while preserving tissue architecture, making it a powerful approach for studying plant developmental transitions. However, preparing small and structurally complex plant tissues for spatial transcriptomics remains technically challenging because samples must be rapidly preserved, precisely oriented, serially sectioned, and accurately positioned within the limited capture area of the Visium slides. Here, we describe an optimized workflow for cryo-embedding, serial cryosectioning, section placement, and data analysis of small
papers.summary: This protocol paper describes an optimized workflow for preparing small, structurally complex plant tissues for 10x Visium spatial transcriptomics. It covers cryo-embedding, serial cryosectioning, precise section placement on capture slides, and downstream data analysis, addressing the technical challenges of rapid preservation and accurate orientation. The method enables genome-wide expression profiling while preserving tissue architecture in plant developmental studies.

papers.title: Marker-Centered Evaluation of De Novo Assemblers Using Validated Microsatellite Loci in the Endangered Korean Fish Pseudopungtungia nigra.
papers.abstract: The recovery of experimentally validated microsatellite loci from short-read assemblies may provide an application-specific measure of assembly quality that complements conventional genome-wide statistics. In this study, four de novo assemblers-SPAdes, ABySS, SOAPdenovo2, and MaSuRCA-were evaluated using genomic reads from two individuals of the endangered Korean freshwater fish Pseudopungtungia nigra. Assembler performance was assessed based on assembly contiguity, BUSCO completeness, computational requirements, and the recovery of 20 PCR-validated microsatellite loci and their flanking regio
papers.summary: The authors compared four de novo genome assemblers (SPAdes, ABySS, SOAPdenovo2, MaSuRCA) on short-read data from the endangered Korean fish Pseudopungtungia nigra, evaluating them not only by standard metrics (contiguity, BUSCO completeness, compute cost) but also by whether they recovered 20 PCR-validated microsatellite loci and their flanking regions. This marker-centered approach offers an application-specific complement to genome-wide assembly statistics for choosing an assembler when the downstream goal is microsatellite marker development.

papers.title: Synthetic Reconstruction and Characterization of Endogenous Bacteriophage Genomes from Desulfovibrio vulgaris.
papers.abstract: Microbiologically influenced corrosion (MIC) caused by sulfate-reducing bacteria (SRB) is a major challenge in industrial infrastructure, yet the limited availability of well-characterized bacteriophages has hindered the development of phage-based strategies for controlling these organisms. Here, we present an integrated genome-guided workflow for the discovery, validation, and synthetic reconstruction of endogenous prophages from the model sulfate-reducing bacterium Desulfovibrio vulgaris Hildenborough. Bioinformatic analysis using PHASTEST identified seven prophage-like regions distributed t
papers.summary: The authors developed a genome-guided workflow to identify, validate, and synthetically reconstruct endogenous prophages from the sulfate-reducing bacterium Desulfovibrio vulgaris Hildenborough, a model organism for microbiologically influenced corrosion. Bioinformatic analysis revealed seven prophage-like regions, and the team successfully reconstructed these phage genomes synthetically. This work expands the limited toolkit of characterized bacteriophages for SRB, potentially enabling phage-based strategies to control corrosion-causing biofilms.

papers.title: Identification of Genes Associated with Gut Microbiota Metabolites in Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus Complicated by Acute Cerebral Infarction Based on Bioinformatics and Mendelian Randomization.
papers.abstract: Background: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) and acute cerebral infarction (ACI) are globally prevalent diseases that impose substantial public health burdens. While gut microbiota (GM) is increasingly recognized to regulate metabolic and immune homeostasis linked to both diseases, its shared genetically predicted microbial taxa and underlying metabolite-gene regulatory mechanisms in T2DM and ACI remain unclear, highlighting the need for systematic investigation. Accordingly, this study aimed to elucidate their regulatory mechanisms. Methods: Transcriptomic datasets, genome-wide association stu
papers.summary: This study integrates transcriptomic data with Mendelian randomization to identify gut microbiota taxa and metabolites that may causally contribute to type 2 diabetes complicated by acute cerebral infarction, and links them to candidate genes. The work nominates shared microbial-metabolite-gene regulatory axes as potential mechanistic explanations for the comorbidity.

papers.title: Re-Analysis on GRCh38 with the MANE Select Transcript Resolves Previously Undetected Biallelic ODAD4 Variants in Primary Ciliary Dyskinesia.
papers.abstract: Molecular diagnosis is highly sensitive to the human genome assembly used in a bioinformatics pipeline. Panels designed on GRCh37 (hg19) inherit its exon annotation, whereas transcript standards and interpretation databases are anchored to GRCh38 (hg38); a coding exon absent from GRCh37 can therefore be neither targeted nor analyzed. We describe two unrelated individuals with primary ciliary dyskinesia (PCD) in whom first-line, GRCh37-based panel sequencing was non-diagnostic. Both were re-analyzed on GRCh38 against the Matched Annotation from NCBI and EMBL-EBI (MANE) Select transcript. In Pat
papers.summary: Two unrelated patients with primary ciliary dyskinesia (PCD) remained undiagnosed after standard GRCh37-based panel sequencing. Re-analysis of their data on GRCh38 using the MANE Select transcript revealed biallelic ODAD4 variants that had been missed because a coding exon present in GRCh38 is absent from GRCh37. The study shows that genome assembly and transcript annotation choices can directly determine whether disease-causing variants are detected.

papers.title: Deep Genomic Characterization of Bacillus subtilis SNUY1 & 168 Using MAYA (Multistage Analysis of Prokaryotic Annotations): An Integrated Snakemake-Based Bioinformatics Pipeline.
papers.abstract: Bacillus subtilis is an extensively characterized Gram-positive bacterium with broad applications in agriculture, biotechnology, and biocontrol. Strain SNUY1, known for its antifungal properties and use as an edible coating, has been completely sequenced and deposited in NCBI (accession: CP199918), making it an important model for genomic and functional characterization. Here, we present the MAYA pipeline, a fully automated, rule-based Snakemake workflow that integrates eighteen bioinformatic tools into a single end-to-end framework. MAYA accepts either raw Illumina paired-end FASTQ reads or p
papers.summary: The authors present MAYA, an automated Snakemake-based pipeline that integrates eighteen bioinformatics tools to perform end-to-end genomic characterization of prokaryotes from raw Illumina reads or assembled genomes. They apply it to Bacillus subtilis strains SNUY1 and 168, providing a deep annotation and comparative genomic analysis of the newly sequenced antifungal strain SNUY1.

papers.title: Nanopore Sequencing for Epigenetic Decoding: Applications, Analytical Constraints, and Translational Prospects.
papers.abstract: Epigenetic regulation involves multiple molecular layers, including DNA and RNA modifications, histone post-translational modifications (PTMs), and chromatin accessibility. These processes contribute to cell identity, development, and disease, but their measurement remains technically challenging because sequence context, molecular modification, chromatin state, and transcript structure are often assayed separately. As a representative third-generation sequencing technology, nanopore sequencing is profoundly reshaping the interpretation of the epigenetic code through its distinctive capabiliti
papers.summary: This review examines how nanopore sequencing can decode multiple epigenetic layers—DNA and RNA modifications, histone marks, and chromatin accessibility—from long native molecules, potentially integrating information that is usually assayed separately. It discusses analytical constraints and translational prospects for using nanopore data in epigenetic research and clinical applications.

papers.title: A step forward in comprehensive nanopore-based forensic profiling of STRs, InDel, SNP and mtDNA for identity and appearance prediction.
papers.abstract: The targeted analysis of diverse DNA markers, including single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs), insertion deletion polymorphisms (InDels) and DNA methylation levels, is central to forensic DNA phenotyping, enabling inference of BGA, appearance traits, and age. Such information is relevant when DNA comparison after conventional DNA profiling fails to identify a person of interest. Recent technological developments allow both genetic and epigenetic markers to be analyzed in long-reads within a single platform such as Oxford Nanopore Technologies (ONT). This approach offers an advantage over trad
papers.summary: This study demonstrates that Oxford Nanopore long-read sequencing can simultaneously analyze multiple forensic DNA marker types—STRs, InDels, SNPs, and mtDNA—along with DNA methylation, enabling both identity profiling and appearance/age prediction from a single platform. The approach offers a more comprehensive forensic profiling workflow than conventional methods that require separate assays for genetic and epigenetic markers.

papers.title: Cell-free DNA fragmentomics and epigenomic profiling in hematologic malignancies: current evidence, translational limitations, and future directions.
papers.abstract: Mutation-based liquid biopsy supports diagnosis and disease monitoring in hematologic malignancies, but interpretation of plasma variants may be complicated by clonal hematopoiesis, treatment-related changes, and nonmalignant blood-cell turnover. This structured narrative review evaluates whether cell-free DNA (cfDNA) fragmentomics, DNA methylation, and 5-hydroxymethylcytosine (5hmC) provide complementary information beyond mutation detection. Direct plasma evidence is most developed for selected fragmentomic and 5hmC applications, although most studies remain retrospective, internally validat
papers.summary: This review examines whether cell-free DNA fragmentomics, methylation, and 5hmC profiling add useful information beyond mutation-based liquid biopsy in hematologic malignancies, where clonal hematopoiesis and treatment effects complicate variant interpretation. The authors find that direct plasma evidence is strongest for selected fragmentomic and 5hmC applications, but most studies are retrospective and internally validated only, limiting translation. They outline remaining evidence gaps and future directions for clinical implementation.

papers.title: AI-Assisted WES Variant Interpretation in Neurodevelopmental Disorders: A Narrative Review of Existing Tools.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Neurodevelopmental disorders (NDDs) comprise a heterogeneous group of conditions characterized by alterations in brain development and function, frequently associated with complex genetic architectures. The widespread implementation of next-generation sequencing, particularly whole-exome sequencing (WES), has substantially increased the identification of potentially disease-associated variants, shifting the major challenge from variant detection to their interpretation and prioritization. This review examines the emerging contribution of artificial intelligence (AI) to W
papers.summary: This narrative review surveys how artificial intelligence tools are being applied to interpret and prioritize variants from whole-exome sequencing in neurodevelopmental disorders. It highlights that the bottleneck has shifted from variant detection to interpretation, and catalogs existing AI-assisted approaches for this task.

papers.title: "A human CHRNA6 3' UTR variant alters the molecular environment and microRNA engagement of the adolescent VTA without changing Chrna6 transcript abundance".
papers.abstract: A single nucleotide polymorphism (rs2304297) in the 3' untranslated region (UTR) of CHRNA6 , encoding the α6 nicotinic acetylcholine receptor subunit, is associated with adolescent smoking behavior. Humanized rats carrying the "C" or "G" allele show sex- and genotype-dependent responses to adolescent nicotine, yet the variant does not alter the protein sequence and the mechanism has remained unknown. We examined the molecular consequences of rs2304297 in vivo in the adolescent ventral tegmental area (VTA). Chrna6 transcript abundance did not differ by genotype, nor did transcript stability or
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This study investigates how a common SNP (rs2304297) in the 3' UTR of the CHRNA6 gene, linked to adolescent smoking, exerts its effects. Using humanized rats, the authors show that the variant does not change Chrna6 transcript levels or stability, but instead alters the local molecular environment and microRNA binding in the adolescent ventral tegmental area, providing a mechanistic explanation for allele-specific nicotine responses.

papers.title: Clinical and Genetic Characterization of a Family with Tooth Agenesis Carrying a Novel LEF1 Variant.
papers.abstract: Background: Tooth agenesis is one of the most common developmental anomalies of the human dentition and may occur either as an isolated trait or as part of a syndromic condition. Advances in genomic technologies have facilitated the identification of genes involved in odontogenesis, including LEF1 (Lymphoid Enhancer-Binding Factor 1), a key transcription factor in the WNT signaling pathway. Methods: Whole exome sequencing (WES) was performed in a proband with non-syndromic tooth agenesis to investigate the underlying genetic cause. Parental segregation analysis was performed through Sanger seq
papers.summary: This study used whole exome sequencing to identify a novel LEF1 variant in a family with non-syndromic tooth agenesis, with Sanger sequencing confirming segregation. The finding adds to the evidence that LEF1, a WNT signaling transcription factor, plays a role in human odontogenesis and expands the mutational spectrum for this developmental anomaly.

papers.title: Structural and Molecular Dynamics Analysis of Human β-Defensin 1 Variants Reveals Distinct Perturbation Signatures.
papers.abstract: Human β-defensin 1 (hBD-1) is a small, disulfide-constrained antimicrobial peptide produced predominantly in the kidney and urogenital tract, where it contributes to epithelial innate defense. Genetic variation in the gene encoding hBD-1 has been associated with altered expression levels and susceptibility to infections, including infection following solid organ transplantation, yet the molecular consequences of coding substitutions in the active, mature form remain largely undefined. Here, we integrate conventional genomics, protein bioinformatics, structural modeling, and molecular dynamics
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This study uses structural modeling and molecular dynamics simulations to analyze how naturally occurring genetic variants in the mature human β-defensin 1 antimicrobial peptide affect its structure and dynamics. The authors identify distinct perturbation signatures for different variants, suggesting molecular mechanisms by which coding substitutions could alter peptide function and infection susceptibility.

papers.title: Systematic evaluation of incomplete penetrance in 4,325 rare disease families reveals divergent transcriptional networks in CHD8 pathology.
papers.abstract: Despite major advances in genomic sequencing and analytical pipelines for rare disorders, more than 50% of affected individuals remain without a molecular diagnosis. One challenge is the interpretation of inherited variants exhibiting incomplete penetrance (IP).
papers.journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
papers.summary: This study systematically evaluates incomplete penetrance in 4,325 rare disease families, addressing a major barrier to molecular diagnosis where inherited variants do not always cause disease. Focusing on CHD8 pathology, the authors identify divergent transcriptional networks associated with penetrant versus non-penetrant variants, offering insights into why some carriers remain unaffected.

papers.title: Beyond molecular snapshots: Regulatory trajectories in dynamic epigenetic regulation.
papers.abstract: Epigenetic regulation is commonly interpreted through molecular markers measured at discrete timepoints. While such approaches have generated important biological insights, they primarily provide static representations of regulatory states and may therefore capture only a limited component of dynamic biological processes. Emerging evidence from chromatin biology, transcriptional regulation and genome organisation suggests that biological regulation unfolds through continuously evolving interactions across multiple molecular layers. This article presents a biological hypothesis and conceptual f
papers.summary: This conceptual paper argues that epigenetic regulation is fundamentally dynamic and cannot be fully understood through static molecular snapshots at discrete timepoints. The authors propose a hypothesis that biological regulation emerges from continuously evolving interactions across multiple molecular layers, and they advocate for trajectory-based frameworks that capture regulatory dynamics over time.

papers.title: Overcoming a diagnostic blindspot: Identifying balanced translocations in Mendelian rare disease cohorts.
papers.abstract: Short-read genome sequencing generates the signal necessary to detect balanced reciprocal translocations at single-nucleotide resolution, but standard structural variant callers represent them as breakend pairs. Structural variant callers produce thousands of breakend records per genome, the majority of which are false positives arising from segmental duplications, repetitive elements, and reference assembly artifacts. This specificity problem has prevented balanced translocation detection from entering routine genome sequencing workflows. We developed a highly specific pipeline to resolve bal
papers.journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
papers.summary: The authors developed a highly specific pipeline to detect balanced reciprocal translocations from short-read genome sequencing data, addressing the problem that standard structural variant callers produce thousands of false-positive breakend records. This enables balanced translocation detection to enter routine genome sequencing workflows for Mendelian rare disease cohorts, overcoming a diagnostic blind spot.

papers.title: Primary-Tumor Transcriptomic Signatures Associated with Circulating Tumor Cells Status in Breast Cancer: From CTC-Negative Remodeling to CTC-Associated Metastatic Programs.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Circulating tumor cells (CTCs) play a central role in metastasis by enabling tumor dissemination through the bloodstream. However, the molecular transition from CTC-negative (CTC-) to CTC-positive (CTC+) states and their associated systemic remodeling remain poorly understood. Methods: We performed a transcriptomic comparison between CTC+, CTC-, and healthy individuals using RNA-seq data and a bioinformatics pipeline. Differentially expressed genes (DEGs) were subjected to functional enrichment, protein-protein interaction (PPI) analysis, survival modeling, and drug pert
papers.summary: This study compared primary breast tumor transcriptomes between patients with and without circulating tumor cells (CTCs) in their blood, using RNA-seq and bioinformatics analyses. It identified gene expression signatures and pathways that distinguish CTC-positive from CTC-negative tumors, and linked these to survival outcomes and potential drug targets. The work suggests a progression from a CTC-negative remodeling state toward CTC-associated metastatic gene programs.

papers.title: Whole-Genome Sequencing Reveals the Resistome, Virulome, Pan-Genome Architecture, and Phylogenomic Diversity of Extensively Drug-Resistant Salmonella enterica Serovar Typhi in Pakistan.
papers.abstract: The emergence of multidrug-resistant (MDR) and extensively drug-resistant (XDR) Salmonella enterica serovar Typhi has severely constrained typhoid treatment. Pakistan is a major hotspot for XDR typhoid, yet genomic evidence defining the molecular basis of antimicrobial resistance, virulence, and genomic diversity of circulating strains remains limited. A cross-sectional study was conducted from January to December 2021 involving 252 culture-confirmed S. Typhi isolates collected from patients with suspected typhoid fever in Peshawar, Pakistan. Isolates were identified by conventional microbiolo
papers.summary: This study performed whole-genome sequencing on 252 culture-confirmed Salmonella Typhi isolates from Peshawar, Pakistan, to characterize the resistome, virulome, pan-genome architecture, and phylogenomic diversity of extensively drug-resistant (XDR) strains. The genomic analysis reveals the molecular basis of antimicrobial resistance and virulence in circulating XDR typhoid strains, addressing a critical gap in genomic surveillance in a major XDR hotspot. The findings provide a comprehensive genomic resource for understanding the evolution and spread of XDR S. Typhi in Pakistan.

papers.title: Ryder: epigenome normalization using a two-tier model and internal reference regions.
papers.abstract: Sequencing-based epigenomic profiling methods are powerful but suffer from technical variability that complicates cross-sample comparisons and can obscure true biological signals. While existing normalization methods using spike-in controls or computational approaches have been proposed, they often rely on assumptions that may not hold across diverse experimental conditions or require additional data types.
papers.summary: Ryder is a new computational normalization method for sequencing-based epigenomic data that uses a two-tier model with internal reference regions to correct technical variability across samples. Unlike spike-in or other computational approaches, it avoids assumptions that may not hold across diverse experimental conditions and does not require additional data types. This enables more reliable cross-sample comparisons and better recovery of true biological signals.

papers.title: HINN prioritizes multi-omics biomarkers associated with cognitive decline.
papers.abstract: Integrating multi-omics data for disease prediction remains challenging due to the complexity of cross-layer biological interactions and the limited use of prior biological knowledge in many machine learning models. We present the Hierarchical Input Neural Network (HINN), a deep learning framework that incorporates biologically informed connections across genomic, epigenetic, and transcriptomic layers to model regulatory relationships in a structured and interpretable manner. HINN was applied to blood-derived multi-omics data to predict cognitive assessment scores, including Mini-Mental State
papers.summary: The authors present HINN, a deep learning framework that uses biologically informed connections across genomic, epigenetic, and transcriptomic layers to model regulatory relationships in an interpretable way. Applied to blood-derived multi-omics data, HINN predicts cognitive assessment scores such as the Mini-Mental State Examination and prioritizes biomarkers associated with cognitive decline. The work offers a structured approach for integrating prior biological knowledge into multi-omics prediction models.

papers.title: DeCTCF: Decoding CTCF binding sequences by leveraging predicted epigenomic features.
papers.abstract: CTCF is a key architectural protein with diverse roles in genome organization and gene regulation, yet how it achieves these roles in different contexts remains unclear. Pretrained sequence-based models such as Sei provide predicted epigenomic features that can be used in downstream analyses of regulatory elements. Here, we developed DeCTCF, an integrative computational framework that uses pretrained Sei predictions to analyze 236,552 CTCF binding sequences by integrating CTCF ChIP-seq data from 118 human cell lines. By leveraging predicted epigenomic features from the Sei model, we grouped th
papers.summary: DeCTCF is a computational framework that uses predicted epigenomic features from the pretrained Sei model to analyze 236,552 CTCF binding sequences across 118 human cell lines. By integrating these predictions with CTCF ChIP-seq data, the authors group binding sequences into distinct clusters, revealing context-dependent patterns in how CTCF achieves its architectural and regulatory roles. The work demonstrates that pretrained sequence models can be repurposed to decode the functional heterogeneity of regulatory elements.

papers.title: A machine learning classifier reveals hidden rare biallelic heterozygous variants in the coding regions of Meniere disease genome.
papers.abstract: Meniere disease (MD) is a rare inner ear disorder with a significant genetic contribution. We developed the MD classifier, an ML tool to distinguish familial from sporadic MD cases using rare variants in coding regions. We have generated a disease-specific gene variant score incorporating gene, variant, and disease-specific features. A gradient boosting classifier achieved the highest performance, with a test AUC of 0.843 (95% CI, 0.702-0.948) and an accuracy of 81.5%. Reclassification of sporadic cases into the familial group ranged from 16.6% to 28.3%. The model identified a burden of bialle
papers.summary: The authors built a machine learning classifier (gradient boosting) that distinguishes familial from sporadic Meniere disease using rare coding variants, achieving a test AUC of 0.843 and 81.5% accuracy. Reclassifying 16.6–28.3% of sporadic cases as familial suggests hidden biallelic heterozygous variant burden in MD. This provides a tool for genetic stratification of MD patients and highlights underappreciated variant architecture.

papers.title: Lysine crotonylation acts as an epigenetic switch for glutamate neurotransmission and spatial memory.
papers.abstract: Histone posttranslational modifications, particularly lysine acetylation (Kac), are critical epigenetic regulators of transcriptional programs underlying long-term memory consolidation. Beyond Kac, several other non-acetyl acylations have been identified with the ability to regulate transcription; however, their role in memory consolidation remains unknown. Here, we identify histone lysine crotonylation (Kcr) as a molecular switch for long-term memory and glutamatergic neurotransmission. We find that spatial learning induces distinct spatiotemporal patterns of Kcr across hippocampal subregions
papers.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
papers.summary: This study identifies histone lysine crotonylation (Kcr), a non-acetyl histone modification, as a key epigenetic regulator of long-term memory consolidation. Spatial learning produces distinct spatiotemporal patterns of Kcr across hippocampal subregions, and Kcr appears to act as a molecular switch controlling glutamatergic neurotransmission and spatial memory. The work extends epigenetic understanding of memory beyond histone acetylation to a broader class of acyl modifications.

papers.title: Long-read sequencing of FLG identifies extensive copy number variation in exon 3 and detects rare loss-of-function variants.
papers.abstract: Loss-of-function (LOF) variants of the FLG gene are risk factors for atopic dermatitis. However, owing to the repetitive nature of exon 3, these variants are difficult to characterize. We sought to determine whether the use of long-read technologies would enable better characterization of the FLG gene and improve the detection of LOF variants. We sequenced a diverse clinical cohort of 192 samples collected in Belgium, Ireland, and Rwanda using long-read sequencing as well as publicly available data. We identified both common and rare LOF variants linked to atopic dermatitis in our clinical coh
papers.journal: JID innovations : skin science from molecules to population health
papers.summary: Using long-read sequencing on 192 clinical samples from Belgium, Ireland, and Rwanda, the authors characterized the repetitive exon 3 of FLG, revealing extensive copy number variation and identifying both common and rare loss-of-function variants associated with atopic dermatitis. Long-read technology overcame the limitations of short-read methods in this repetitive region, improving detection of disease-relevant variants.

papers.title: MLMP: A Methylation-Associated lncRNA-mRNA Prognostic Signature for Endometrial Carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Endometrial carcinoma (EC) is one of the most common gynecological malignancies. Aberrant DNA methylation (DNAm) is an important epigenetic alteration involved in cancer progression. Long non-coding RNAs (LncRNAs) play critical roles in gene regulation and pathological processes. However, the biological and prognostic significance of lncRNA-mRNA pairs associated with methylation remains unclear.
papers.summary: This study develops MLMP, a prognostic signature for endometrial carcinoma based on methylation-associated lncRNA-mRNA pairs. The authors identify DNA methylation-linked lncRNA-mRNA interactions and use them to build a model predicting patient outcomes, highlighting the epigenetic regulation of non-coding RNAs in cancer progression.

papers.title: Epigenetic Insights in Pediatric Multiple Sclerosis: DNA Methylation Highlights an Involvement of Epstein-Barr Virus Infection and Host Immune Networks.
papers.abstract: Pediatric-onset multiple sclerosis (PedMS) provides a unique opportunity to investigate MS pathogenesis because of the short interval between environmental exposures and disease onset. This study aimed to identify differentially methylated regions (DMRs) that mediate the interplay between environmental triggers and genomic factors in the early stages of the disease.
papers.summary: This study identifies differentially methylated DNA regions in pediatric-onset multiple sclerosis, a form of MS with a short interval between environmental exposure and disease onset. The methylation changes point to Epstein-Barr virus infection and host immune networks as key players in early disease pathogenesis.

papers.title: Diverse patterns of transcriptional regulation and epigenetic reprogramming within PMDs contribute to ESCC progression by regulating EMT and immunosuppression.
papers.abstract: Partially methylated domains (PMDs) represent extensive genome-wide hypomethylated regions that drive genomic instability and proto-oncogene activation. However, their complex regulatory influence on tumor-specific transcriptional networks remains largely elusive. In this study, we developed a robust computational pipeline to characterize aberrant PMD landscapes across pan-cancer. We specifically focused on the epigenetic features associated with transcriptional dysregulation in esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC). By analyzing gene expression patterns, we classified PMDs into four disti
papers.summary: The authors built a computational pipeline to map partially methylated domains (PMDs) across cancers and applied it to esophageal squamous cell carcinoma, classifying PMDs into four distinct subtypes based on their gene expression patterns. These PMD subtypes show different epigenetic features and appear to regulate epithelial-mesenchymal transition and immune suppression, linking large-scale hypomethylation to tumor progression.

papers.title: Controlling for DNA dosage with whole-genome sequencing improves ATAC-seq peak calling.
papers.abstract: ATAC-seq is a powerful method for mapping chromatin accessibility and identifying cis-regulatory elements (CREs) across cell types. We reveal that ATAC-seq peak calling is compromised by local biases in DNA dosage, arising from copy number variations but also from DNA replication timing. As part of the FANTOM consortium's efforts, we propose enhancing the model-based analysis of ChIP-seq pipeline by integrating whole-genome sequencing (WGS) data, analogous to input controls in ChIP-seq analyses. This adjustment increases both the number and width of ATAC peaks, with improved proximity to trans
papers.summary: ATAC-seq peak calling is biased by local variation in DNA copy number and replication timing, which can create false or distorted accessibility signals. The authors show that incorporating whole-genome sequencing data as an input control, analogous to ChIP-seq input controls, corrects for these DNA dosage biases and yields more and wider ATAC peaks that better align with regulatory elements.

papers.title: pycircdb: integrated circRNA database annotation for computational workflows.
papers.abstract: Currently, multiple databases exist for the annotation of circular RNAs, providing descriptions of their genomic features, FASTA sequences, predicted microRNA targets and RNA-binding protein interactions. Despite the availability of these resources, annotation remains cumbersome. Conflicting identifiers and genomic coordinates for circular RNAs across databases pose a challenge to reproducibility for users. Furthermore, current databases primarily provide access via web-based graphical user interfaces, bulk downloads and limited programmatic access, rendering their use in computational workflo
papers.summary: pycircdb is a new Python package that integrates multiple circRNA databases into a single programmatic interface, resolving conflicting identifiers and genomic coordinates across sources. It enables reproducible, scriptable annotation of circRNAs—including sequences, microRNA targets, and RNA-binding protein interactions—directly within computational workflows. This addresses the current reliance on web GUIs and bulk downloads that hinders automated analysis.

papers.title: Integrating multi-omics with machine learning: from genomic variant functional annotation to pharmacogenomics and biomarker discovery.
papers.abstract: Integrating heterogeneous multi-omics data with machine learning (ML) provides a powerful framework for interpreting genomic variants and advancing pharmacogenomic research in precision medicine. High-throughput technologies have generated vast datasets spanning genomics, transcriptomics, epigenomics, and proteomics, yet integrating these high-dimensional data into clinically meaningful insights remains a major computational challenge. Machine learning and deep learning models, including Graph Neural Networks (GNNs), Transformers, and Variational Autoencoders (VAEs), offer promising solutions.
papers.summary: This review surveys how machine learning and deep learning models—including graph neural networks, transformers, and variational autoencoders—are being applied to integrate multi-omics data for genomic variant functional annotation, pharmacogenomics, and biomarker discovery. It frames the integration of high-dimensional genomics, transcriptomics, epigenomics, and proteomics data as a major computational challenge for precision medicine and highlights emerging model architectures as promising solutions.

papers.title: Strategic roadmap for FAIR-compliant transcriptomic workflows: from technical challenges to bioinformatics democratization.
papers.abstract: This article draws on the authors' more than 17 years of experience in transcriptomic research, beginning with the introduction of high-throughput sequencing in Mexico in 2009. Here, we provide a critical review of bioinformatics pipelines for different RNA classes, ranging from small RNAs to long non-coding RNAs. Our analysis encompasses a range of scenarios, from de novo transcriptome assembly for organisms lacking a closely related and adequately annotated reference genome to differential expression analysis based on a well-annotated reference genome. By providing a comprehensive overview o
papers.summary: This review draws on 17+ years of transcriptomic research experience to critically assess bioinformatics pipelines for different RNA classes, from small RNAs to long non-coding RNAs, covering scenarios from de novo assembly without a good reference genome to differential expression with a well-annotated one. The authors frame these technical challenges within a FAIR-compliant workflow roadmap aimed at democratizing bioinformatics access, particularly in resource-limited settings.

papers.title: gTranslate: rapid and accurate translation table prediction for prokaryotic genomes.
papers.abstract: Bioinformatic tools often require the prediction of protein-coding genes to make inferences about prokaryotic genomes. Typically, the genetic code used for translating genes to proteins must be specified by the user based on the taxonomic classification of a genome assembly or, for some widely used tools, established using a heuristic rule based on gene coding densities. Manual specification is at best inconvenient, but more challenging is that many bioinformatic tools are applied before taxonomic classifications have been established making specifying the translation table impractical.
papers.summary: gTranslate is a new tool that predicts the correct genetic code (translation table) for prokaryotic genomes directly from sequence data, without requiring prior taxonomic classification. This addresses a common bottleneck in gene prediction pipelines where the translation table must be specified manually or guessed via heuristics. The tool is presented as rapid and accurate, making it useful for automated annotation workflows.

papers.title: PoLoCo: a reproducible pooled low-coverage workflow for draft genome assembly and allele frequency analysis from ethanol-preserved small non-model invertebrates.
papers.abstract: Many ecologically important small invertebrates are preserved in ethanol, which compromises DNA integrity and severely limits their potential to be utilized in further genomic research. The lack of soil arthropod representation ultimately results in limited availability of reference genomes and population genomic inference from pooled sequencing (Pool-seq).
papers.summary: PoLoCo is a reproducible workflow for generating draft genome assemblies and allele frequency estimates from pooled, low-coverage sequencing of small non-model invertebrates preserved in ethanol. It addresses the challenge of degraded DNA in ethanol-preserved soil arthropods, a group poorly represented in reference genome databases, enabling population genomic inference where it was previously difficult.

papers.title: A methodology to identify a DNA methylation-based signature of prenatal air pollution exposure in the ECHO Cohort.
papers.abstract: Prenatal exposure to ambient air pollutants has been associated with adverse child health across different populations. In the absence of direct air pollution exposure measures, epigenetic biomarkers can serve as indicators of cumulative exposure. Previously, we developed a methodological pipeline to build a prediction model to distinguish infants highly exposed to air pollutants in utero based on DNA methylation in cord blood samples. Here, we test and refine this pipeline using data from multiple pregnancy cohort sites included in the Environmental influences on Child Health Outcomes (ECHO)
papers.summary: This paper tests and refines a methodological pipeline for building DNA methylation-based prediction models that distinguish infants with high versus low prenatal air pollution exposure using cord blood samples. Using data from multiple ECHO pregnancy cohort sites, the work aims to establish epigenetic biomarkers as proxies for cumulative air pollution exposure when direct measurements are unavailable.

papers.title: The double-edged sword of TOX: orchestrating T cell exhaustion and epigenetic remodeling in the tumor microenvironment.
papers.abstract: The capacity to profoundly change chromatin domains and in turn drive or inhibit gene expression makes chromatin modulators a powerful tool adopted to regulate crucial steps during development and cell lineage specification. These proteins can however be as well engaged to irreversibly reprogram cells toward pathological outcomes such as cancer. An example of such chromatin remodelers is the family of Thymocyte-selection associated high mobility box proteins (TOX), which has rather pleiotropic functions during development and in cancer. In light of the most recent findings, this review gives a
papers.summary: This review examines the TOX family of chromatin remodelers, which have dual roles in both normal development and cancer progression. The authors synthesize recent findings on how TOX proteins orchestrate T cell exhaustion and epigenetic remodeling within the tumor microenvironment, highlighting their pleiotropic functions and potential as therapeutic targets.
